intent.raw_query: Eastern Europe city hop Prague + Budapest, $1200, 8 days, September 2026

experiences.name: Prague Castle Complex Tour
experiences.description: Explore the largest ancient castle complex in the world, including St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and Golden Lane. Walk through centuries of Bohemian history with stunning panoramic views over Prague's red-roofed skyline.

experiences.name: Budapest Thermal Bath Experience at Széchenyi
experiences.description: Soak in one of Europe's largest and most iconic thermal bath complexes, built in 1913 in stunning Neo-Baroque style. A deeply cultural Hungarian tradition that blends relaxation, architecture, and local social life all in one visit.

experiences.name: Danube River Evening Cruise
experiences.description: Glide along the Danube at sunset and witness Budapest's illuminated Parliament Building, Buda Castle, and Chain Bridge — a UNESCO World Heritage panorama. An unforgettable way to absorb the city's grandeur from the water.

experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Jewish Quarter Walking Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval Old Town Square, marvel at the Astronomical Clock, and explore Josefov — one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish quarters with six historic synagogues and a hauntingly beautiful cemetery dating to the 15th century.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Discover Budapest's legendary ruin bars born in abandoned buildings of the Jewish Quarter, starting with the iconic Szimpla Kert. Sample Hungarian street food like lángos (fried dough) and kürtőskalács (chimney cake) while soaking in the city's vibrant nightlife culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight LH lands at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the airport bus (Line 119) to Nádraží Veleslavín metro station, then Metro Line A to Malostranská or Hradčanská stop. Check into your Hradčany district boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Hradčany Neighborhood on Foot: Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Archbishop's Palace exterior, and walk down Nerudova Street with its charming baroque townhouses. Peek at the Prague Castle gates and outer courtyards (free to enter) to get your bearings for a deeper visit later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Walk on Petřín Hill: Take the short walk or tram to Petřín Hill for panoramic golden-hour views over Prague's red rooftops and the Vltava River. Wind down with a relaxed stroll back through Malá Strana (Lesser Town).

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Lokál Malá Strana (Míšeňská 12) — affordable Czech pub food; try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) with bread dumplings for around 180–220 CZK (~€7–9).
meals.dinner: U Hrocha (Thunovská 10) — classic Czech pub near Malá Strana, hearty goulash and local Pilsner Urquell on tap, budget-friendly at ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8) per dish.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Buy a 24-hour public transport pass (120 CZK) at the airport to cover all metro and tram rides today. Validate your ticket before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Prague Castle Complex: Arrive early (gates open at 6:00, attractions from 9:00) to beat crowds. Buy the Short Visit Circuit ticket (~250 CZK/~€10) covering St. Vitus Cathedral, Old Royal Palace, and St. George's Basilica. Spend 2–3 hours exploring this UNESCO-listed hilltop fortress — the largest ancient castle in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Golden Lane & Lobkowicz Palace: Walk Golden Lane (Zlatá ulička), the colorful row of tiny medieval cottages once home to castle guards and alchemists (included in ticket). Then visit the independently-owned Lobkowicz Palace (~275 CZK/~€11) for stunning art collections and free audio guide narrated by the Lobkowicz family themselves.
day_by_day.evening: Charles Bridge at Dusk: Descend from the castle through the castle steps or Nerudova Street to Charles Bridge. Walk the iconic 14th-century bridge lined with 30 baroque statues as the lanterns flicker on. Enjoy buskers and atmospheric views of the illuminated castle above.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style morning at Kavárna Nový Svět (Nový Svět street, Hradčany) — a hidden gem near the hotel; coffee + toast for ~80–100 CZK (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local potraviny (grocery store) near the castle — grab fresh bread, local cheese, and fruit for under 100 CZK (~€4). Eat in the castle gardens.
meals.dinner: Restaurace U Zlaté Hrušky (Nový Svět 3) — a cozy Hradčany restaurant with Czech classics; budget ~250–300 CZK (~€10–12) for a main and a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle is best explored in the morning before tour groups arrive. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the cobblestones are uneven. The castle gardens close at 18:00 in September, so plan garden visits before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Old Town (Staré Město) Exploration: Take Metro Line A to Staroměstská. Visit the Old Town Square and watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour — free to watch from outside. Climb the Old Town Hall Tower (~150 CZK/~€6) for sweeping views over the terracotta rooftops. Explore the Jan Hus Memorial and surrounding Gothic and Baroque architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jewish Quarter (Josefov): Walk through the historic Jewish Quarter, one of the best-preserved in Europe. The exterior of the synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery can be viewed from the street for free. If budget allows, a combined ticket to enter the synagogues and cemetery is ~550 CZK (~€22) — worthwhile for history lovers. Alternatively, stroll Pařížská Street and absorb the neighborhood's layered history.
day_by_day.evening: Vinohrady or Žižkov Neighborhood Bar Crawl: Take the metro to Náměstí Míru or Žižkov for Prague's authentic local bar scene. Visit a traditional hospoda (pub) like Pivovarský Klub for craft Czech beer from ~45–60 CZK per half-liter. Enjoy the local atmosphere away from tourist crowds.

meals.breakfast: Chlebíčky (open-faced sandwiches) from a local deli or Albert supermarket near Old Town — classic Czech breakfast for ~50–80 CZK (~€2–3).
meals.lunch: Maitrea (Týnská ulička 6) — vegetarian Czech-fusion restaurant near Old Town Square; filling lunch menu for ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8).
meals.dinner: Lokál Dlouhááá (Dlouhá 33) — one of Prague's best budget Czech pubs; unfiltered Pilsner Urquell tank beer and svíčková or roast pork for ~200–250 CZK (~€8–10).

day_by_day.notes: September 17 is a regular weekday — the Astronomical Clock show happens every hour on the hour. Josefov can be explored meaningfully even without paid entry by reading the historical plaques and walking the streets. Budget travelers can skip the interior tickets and still gain a strong sense of the quarter's history.

day_by_day.morning: Vyšehrad Fortress: Take Metro Line C to Vyšehrad station. Explore this lesser-visited but historically rich fortress overlooking the Vltava — free to enter the grounds. Visit the Vyšehrad Cemetery where Czech luminaries like Dvořák and Mucha are buried (free), and the Romanesque Rotunda of St. Martin. Enjoy peaceful gardens with city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wenceslas Square & National Museum: Walk or metro to Václavské náměstí. Stroll the grand boulevard, see the St. Wenceslas equestrian statue, and visit the National Museum (~200 CZK/~€8) at the top of the square — recently renovated with impressive natural history and Czech history collections. Explore the surrounding New Town (Nové Město) streets.
day_by_day.evening: Prague Night Train to Budapest: Pack your bags and head to Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station). Board the overnight EuroNight or Regiojet/FlixTrain sleeper train to Budapest Keleti. Budget sleeper/couchette tickets can be booked from ~€20–40 in advance. Overnight journey takes approximately 7–8 hours.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a koláč (Czech pastry) from Café Savoy or a local bakery near your hotel for ~80–120 CZK (~€3–5).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Dlouhá 39) — legendary Prague butcher-restaurant; try the beef tartare or pork schnitzel sandwich for ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8).
meals.dinner: Pack train snacks from Albert or Billa supermarket near the main station — sandwiches, fruit, snacks, and a local beer for the overnight journey (~100–150 CZK/~€4–6 total).

day_by_day.notes: Check train schedules and book overnight train tickets in advance at cd.cz (Czech Railways), Regiojet.com, or FlixTrain. A couchette (shared sleeping compartment) is the most budget-friendly option. Keep your valuables secure overnight. This is your final night in Prague — do a last check of your Hradčany accommodation before heading to the station.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive Budapest & Check In: Arrive at Budapest Keleti station around 8:00–9:00. Take Metro Line 2 (red line) to reach central Pest. Check into your Budapest accommodation (book a budget hostel or guesthouse in the 7th or 8th district for ~€15–25/night). Freshen up and head out to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Andrássy Avenue & Heroes' Square: Walk or metro to Hősök tere (Heroes' Square) — free to visit. Marvel at the Millennium Monument with statues of the seven Magyar chieftains and Hungarian kings. Stroll back along the grand UNESCO-listed Andrássy Avenue, Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées, passing the Hungarian State Opera House (exterior free, tours available ~€10).
day_by_day.evening: Ruin Bar District (Romkocsmák): Budapest's legendary 7th District ruin bars are a must. Start at Szimpla Kert (Kazinczy u. 14) — the original ruin bar set in a crumbling pre-war building filled with eclectic art and local craft beer (~800–1200 HUF/~€2–3 per beer). Walk to Fogasház or Instant for more of the same vibrant scene.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the train or grab a fresh lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) from a street vendor near Keleti station for ~600–800 HUF (~€1.50–2).
meals.lunch: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje (Király u. 55) — a beloved Hungarian canteen (kifőzde) with daily home-cooked specials like goulash soup and stuffed peppers for ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–5).
meals.dinner: Karavan Street Food Court (Kazinczy u. 18, next to Szimpla) — outdoor street food with burgers, langos, and chimney cakes; budget ~1,500–2,500 HUF (~€4–7).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Budapest 24-hour public transport pass (~2,500 HUF/~€7) at Keleti station — it covers metro, trams, and buses. The ruin bar scene is busiest on Friday and Saturday nights, so tonight is perfect timing. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded bars.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle & Castle District: Take Metro Line 2 to Batthyány tér, then walk across the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) or take the funicular (~1,200 HUF one way) up to Buda Castle Hill. Explore the Hungarian National Gallery (free on Sundays for EU citizens, ~3,200 HUF otherwise) and the historic Castle District streets. Visit Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) — exterior free, terrace ~1,200 HUF — for iconic panoramic views over the Danube and Parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Matthias Church & Gellért Hill: Visit Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) inside the Castle District (~2,500 HUF/~€7) with its stunning neo-Gothic interior and colorful Zsolnay tile roof. Then hike or take Bus 27 to Gellért Hill (Gellért-hegy) for the best 360° panorama of Budapest from the Citadella fortress — free to visit.
day_by_day.evening: Great Market Hall & Vaci Street: Take Tram 47 or 49 to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — browse the ground floor for fresh produce, Hungarian paprika, and local sausages (closes around 17:00 on Sundays). Stroll along the Danube promenade at dusk and watch the Parliament building light up across the river.

meals.breakfast: Molnár's Kürtőskalács (multiple locations) — chimney cake fresh off the spit for ~700–900 HUF (~€2) with a coffee from a nearby espresso bar.
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró (Steindl Imre u. 13) — authentic Hungarian classics near the Parliament; gulyás (goulash) and chicken paprikash for ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€7–10).
meals.dinner: Bors GasztroBar (Kazinczy u. 10) — cult-favorite tiny soup and sandwich bar in the Jewish Quarter; enormous portions for ~1,500–2,000 HUF (~€4–6). Expect a short queue — worth it.

day_by_day.notes: September Sundays can see larger crowds at Buda Castle — arrive before 10:00 for a quieter experience. The Great Market Hall closes early on Sundays (around 15:00–17:00), so plan accordingly. The Danube promenade is magical at sunset — bring a light jacket as September evenings in Budapest can be cool (~14–18°C).

day_by_day.morning: Hungarian Parliament Building: Book a guided tour in advance at parlament.hu (~8,000 HUF/~€22 for non-EU citizens, or ~4,000 HUF for EU citizens — budget splurge worth it). The 45-minute tour includes the ornate main staircase, the Hungarian Crown Jewels, and the stunning domed hall. Arrive early for your timed entry slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Széchenyi Thermal Bath: Budapest's famous thermal baths are a cultural institution. Széchenyi (Állatkerti krt. 11) is the largest and most iconic — outdoor pools, indoor thermal pools, and chess-playing locals. Entry ~7,500–9,000 HUF (~€20–25) including locker. Alternatively, the slightly cheaper Rudas Baths (~5,000 HUF) offer a more authentic, less touristy experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dohány Street Synagogue & Jewish Quarter Walk: Visit the Great Synagogue (Dohány utcai Zsinagóga) — the largest in Europe (~5,000 HUF/~€14). Explore the surrounding 7th District (Erzsébetváros) Jewish Quarter on foot, visiting the Holocaust Memorial Tree of Life in the synagogue garden and the atmospheric Gozsdu Udvar courtyard passage filled with bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud (Vörösmarty tér 7) — a Budapest institution since 1858; treat yourself to a coffee and slice of Dobos torte (~2,500–3,500 HUF/~€7–10) as a one-time splurge.
meals.lunch: Vapiano Budapest (Váci u. 13) — fresh pasta and pizza made to order; budget ~2,500–3,000 HUF (~€7–8) for a filling meal.
meals.dinner: Kőleves Vendéglő (Kazinczy u. 37) — 'Stone Soup' restaurant in the Jewish Quarter; warm, community-style atmosphere with Hungarian-Jewish cuisine for ~3,000–4,000 HUF (~€8–11) per main.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Parliament tour online well in advance — slots fill up quickly, especially on weekends. The thermal bath afternoon is a perfect mid-trip reset for tired legs. Bring flip-flops, a swimsuit, and a small towel (or rent one at the baths for ~500 HUF). The Synagogue closes early on Fridays and is closed Saturdays — Monday is ideal.

day_by_day.morning: Margaret Island (Margit-sziget): Take Tram 4 or 6 to Margit híd and walk onto the car-free island in the middle of the Danube. Rent a four-wheel bike (~2,500 HUF/hour) or walk the scenic loop past the medieval monastery ruins, Japanese garden, musical fountain, and Palatinus Strand beach. A peaceful, free green escape in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Budapest History Museum & Souvenir Shopping: Return to Pest for last-minute exploration. Visit the Budapest History Museum in Buda Castle (~2,800 HUF/~€8) for a deep dive into the city's layered Roman, medieval, and modern history. Then browse the Great Market Hall's upper floor for affordable Hungarian souvenirs — paprika, Tokaji wine, embroidered tablecloths, and Herend porcelain replicas.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Danube Evening Walk: Enjoy a final sunset walk along the Danube embankment (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, watching the Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and Parliament all illuminated simultaneously — one of Europe's most spectacular urban night views. Celebrate your 8-day Eastern European adventure with a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fröhlich Cukrászda (Dob u. 22) — a historic Jewish bakery in the 7th District; try flódni (layered apple-walnut-poppy seed pastry) and coffee for ~1,000–1,500 HUF (~€3–4).
meals.lunch: Picnic on Margaret Island — grab supplies from a nearby CBA or Spar supermarket; sandwiches, local cheese, and fruit for ~1,500 HUF (~€4).
meals.dinner: Mazel Tov (Akácfa u. 47) — stunning ruin-bar-style Middle Eastern restaurant in the Jewish Quarter; mezze plates and cocktails in an unforgettable setting; budget ~4,000–5,500 HUF (~€11–15) for a proper send-off meal.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is on September 22, plan your airport transfer from Budapest Keleti or Deák Ferenc tér via the 100E airport express bus (~2,200 HUF one way, ~30 minutes to BUD Airport). Leave at least 2.5 hours before departure. If departing later or the next day, use this final evening for any missed sights or a final thermal bath visit. Total estimated daily spend in Budapest: ~€30–50/day excluding accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Hradčany district boutique hotel via airport express bus or taxi (~45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a neighborhood walk around Hradčany.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle introduction to Hradčany: stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Archbishop's Palace and Schwarzenberg Palace exteriors. Walk down Nerudova Street, soaking in the baroque architecture and artisan shops. No heavy touring — save energy after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner near the hotel, then a relaxed evening walk to catch the golden-hour glow over the city from the Hradčany viewpoints above the Vltava River.

meals.breakfast: Skip (in-flight meal assumed) or grab a coffee and pastry at a café near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bite at a local bakery or café in Hradčany — try a traditional chlebíček (open-faced sandwich) and soup for ~5–8 EUR.
meals.dinner: Lokál Hradčany or U Zlaté Hrušky — mid-range Czech cuisine; try svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) or roast duck. Budget ~20–30 EUR per person with a beer.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Focus on settling in and acclimatizing to the neighborhood rather than rushing to major sights.

day_by_day.morning: Full Prague Castle Complex exploration (9:00–12:30): Visit St. Vitus Cathedral (stunning Gothic interior), the Old Royal Palace, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane (tiny medieval houses). Purchase the combined ticket (~15 EUR) for full access. Arrive early to beat the midday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most) on foot, pausing at each baroque statue. Continue into the Old Town (Staré Město): visit the Old Town Square, watch the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) strike the hour, and explore the Týn Church. Browse the surrounding streets and pop into a bookshop or gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Old Town, then an evening river cruise on the Vltava for illuminated views of the castle and bridges (~15–20 EUR for a 1-hour cruise). End the night with a craft beer at a riverside bar.

meals.breakfast: Café Louvre-style breakfast at a Hradčany café — coffee, eggs, and toast (~7–10 EUR).
meals.lunch: Café Savoy (Malá Strana) — elegant but mid-range; try their famous sourdough bread and Czech soup (~15 EUR).
meals.dinner: Mincovna Restaurant on Old Town Square — solid Czech and European menu, great atmosphere; ~25–35 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), ideal for walking. Wear comfortable shoes — cobblestones are everywhere. Prague Castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world, so pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Jewish Quarter (Josefov) deep dive (9:00–12:00): Visit the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Old-New Synagogue (Europe's oldest active synagogue, built 1270), and the Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial of 80,000 names inscribed on the walls. Combined ticket ~20 EUR. Deeply moving and historically essential.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — a more local, less touristy side of Prague. Visit the iconic Žižkov Television Tower (with its famous crawling baby sculptures), go up for panoramic city views (~13 EUR). Browse the antique shops and vintage markets along Náměstí Míru.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music concert — Prague is famous for evening chamber concerts in historic venues (churches, palaces). Check listings for concerts at St. Nicholas Church or the Municipal House (~20–30 EUR). Dinner before the concert in Vinohrady.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a neighborhood bakery — grab a koláč (Czech pastry) and coffee (~5–8 EUR).
meals.lunch: Nase Maso (Our Meat) in Old Town — a beloved local butcher-deli hybrid; try the beef tartare or goulash sandwich (~10–12 EUR).
meals.dinner: Eska Restaurant in Žižkov — modern Czech cuisine with a farm-to-table approach; ~25–35 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Jewish Quarter requires respectful attire (shoulders and knees covered). Book concert tickets in advance online — September is peak season and performances sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kutná Hora (1 hour by train, ~5 EUR each way): Visit the famous Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, one of the most extraordinary and macabre sights in Europe. Then visit the magnificent St. Barbara's Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage Gothic masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kutná Hora's medieval silver-mining town center: walk the historic streets, visit the Italian Court (former royal mint), and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of this lesser-visited gem. Return to Prague by late afternoon (~16:00–17:00).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Malá Strana (Lesser Town): wander the quiet baroque streets, visit the Wallenstein Garden (free, closes at dusk), and enjoy a leisurely dinner. This is your last full evening in Prague — savor it.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Prague's Hlavní nádraží (main train station) café before the morning train (~6–8 EUR).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora — Restaurace Dačický, a historic tavern in the town center; try the local game or pork dishes (~12–18 EUR).
meals.dinner: U Malého Glena (Malá Strana) — cozy wine bar and bistro; excellent Czech and Mediterranean small plates; ~20–28 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Trains to Kutná Hora depart from Prague's Hlavní nádraží approximately every hour. The Bone Church is a 10-minute walk from Kutná Hora Sedlec train station. Kutná Hora town center is a further 3 km — take a local bus or taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Prague hotel. Morning free time for last-minute shopping or a final coffee on Charles Bridge before departure. Take the RegioJet or FlixBus to Budapest (approximately 7–8 hours, ~25–40 EUR) or a flight (~1 hour, ~50–100 EUR). Scenic train/bus journey passes through beautiful Central European countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest mid-to-late afternoon. Check into your Budapest accommodation. Take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube riverbank in Pest — the Parliament Building views from the embankment are spectacular, especially in late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Budapest: walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd), climb up to the Buda Castle viewpoint for panoramic city and river views at dusk. Dinner in the Castle District (Várnegyed).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a Prague café before checkout (~7–10 EUR).
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus/train — pack food or buy at a stop en route.
meals.dinner: Rivalda Restaurant in Budapest's Castle District — elegant but accessible; Hungarian classics like goulash and duck leg; ~25–35 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: The RegioJet bus from Prague to Budapest is comfortable, has Wi-Fi, and is very popular — book in advance. If flying, budget extra time for airport transfers on both ends. September is a beautiful time to arrive in Budapest with warm, golden light.

day_by_day.morning: Buda Castle Hill deep dive (9:00–12:30): Explore the Royal Palace (housing the Hungarian National Gallery — free entry to permanent collections), Matthias Church with its dazzling geometric tile roof, and the Fisherman's Bastion (free access to lower terraces, ~3 EUR for upper towers). Incredible panoramic views over the Danube and Pest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to Pest side: explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — Budapest's stunning 19th-century iron market hall. Browse local paprika, salami, folk crafts, and lángos (deep-fried flatbread). Walk along Váci Street and Vörösmarty Square. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House exterior (or book a guided tour for ~15 EUR).
day_by_day.evening: Ruin bar experience in the Jewish Quarter (District VII): Start at Szimpla Kert — Budapest's most famous ruin bar, housed in a crumbling pre-war building filled with eclectic décor. Have dinner at a nearby restaurant first, then explore the ruin bar scene for drinks.

meals.breakfast: Café Gerbeaud on Vörösmarty Square — Budapest's most iconic café; coffee and cake (~10–12 EUR, a splurge but iconic).
meals.lunch: Lángos and fresh produce snacks at the Great Market Hall (~5–8 EUR) — the authentic Budapest street food experience.
meals.dinner: Borkonyha WineKitchen (near the Basilica) — Michelin-starred but surprisingly mid-range lunch/dinner; or opt for Menza on Liszt Ferenc Square for reliable Hungarian bistro food (~20–30 EUR).

day_by_day.notes: Szimpla Kert opens daily — Sunday mornings they host a charming farmers' market if you'd like to visit then instead. The Jewish Quarter is walkable and safe; this neighborhood also contains the Great Synagogue (second largest in the world).

day_by_day.morning: Hungarian Parliament Building guided tour (9:00–11:00, ~25 EUR) — one of the most spectacular neo-Gothic buildings in the world, with the Hungarian Holy Crown on display. Book tickets online in advance. Afterward, walk along the Danube Promenade and visit the haunting Shoes on the Danube memorial.
day_by_day.afternoon: Thermal bath experience at Széchenyi Thermal Bath (the largest in Europe, housed in a stunning neo-baroque building in City Park) — ~22 EUR entry. Soak in the famous outdoor pools and indoor thermal baths. This is quintessential Budapest. Afterward, stroll through City Park (Városliget) and visit Vajdahunyad Castle (free exterior).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Danube (~20–25 EUR for 1–2 hours) — Budapest is arguably the most beautiful city in Europe from the water at night, with the Parliament, Chain Bridge, and Castle all illuminated. Dinner after the cruise in the Gozsdu Courtyard area.

meals.breakfast: Neighborhood café near your accommodation — Hungarian breakfast with cold cuts, cheese, eggs, and fresh bread (~8–10 EUR).
meals.lunch: Bagolyvár Restaurant in City Park (near Széchenyi Baths) — traditional Hungarian home cooking in a charming setting; ~15–20 EUR.
meals.dinner: Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Courtyard) — a lively passage lined with restaurants and bars; try a Hungarian-fusion restaurant or a wine bar with charcuterie; ~20–28 EUR per person.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and towel for the thermal baths (or rent towels on-site for ~2–3 EUR). Széchenyi is busy but manageable on weekday afternoons. Book the Danube cruise in advance for September — it's peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai Zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world, with a moving Holocaust memorial garden (the Weeping Willow sculpture). ~15 EUR entry. Explore the adjacent Jewish Museum. Walk through the historic Jewish Quarter streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Budapest exploration: visit St. Stephen's Basilica (free entry, ~5 EUR for dome climb with panoramic views), browse the nearby upscale shopping street of Andrássy Avenue (Budapest's Champs-Élysées, a UNESCO World Heritage site), and stop at the House of Terror Museum (~12 EUR) — a sobering but essential museum documenting Hungary's fascist and communist regimes in the actual building that served as both headquarters.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Budapest — choose a special restaurant to mark the end of the journey. Return to accommodation, pack, and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian breakfast — try a neighborhood pékség (bakery) for fresh kifli (crescent rolls) with butter and jam, and a strong espresso (~4–6 EUR).
meals.lunch: Stand25 Bistro in the Jewish Quarter — beloved local bistro with creative Hungarian dishes; ~15–20 EUR.
meals.dinner: Onyx Restaurant (splurge option, Michelin-starred, ~60–80 EUR) OR Costes Downtown (mid-range splurge, ~40–50 EUR) for a memorable farewell meal — both serve elevated Hungarian cuisine with exceptional wine lists.

day_by_day.notes: The House of Terror is intense and emotionally heavy — allow 1.5–2 hours and be prepared for confronting content. If you prefer a lighter final afternoon, substitute with a leisurely walk on Margaret Island (Margit-sziget) — a peaceful green island in the middle of the Danube, free to enter. Check departure logistics the night before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Eastern Europe (Prague + Budapest) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Prague Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Václav Havel Airport to your boutique hotel in Hradčany district. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your elegantly appointed room with views of the castle quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the Hradčany district. Stroll along Hradčanské náměstí (Hradčany Square), admire the Archbishop's Palace façade, and explore the charming cobblestone lanes of Nový Svět (New World), one of Prague's most picturesque and peaceful neighborhoods. Stop at the Loreto Prague — a stunning Baroque pilgrimage site with a treasury of ornate religious artifacts — for a relaxed 45-minute visit.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk to the Royal Garden terrace near Prague Castle for sweeping panoramic views over the red rooftops of Malá Strana and the Vltava River. Dinner at a premium Hradčany-area restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana — a beautifully restored Neo-Renaissance café offering refined Czech classics, open sandwiches, and excellent coffee. Perfect for a first taste of Prague.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coda Restaurant (Aria Hotel, Malá Strana) — a Michelin-recognized fine dining experience with seasonal Czech and European cuisine, exceptional wine list, and intimate ambiance just a short walk from Hradčany.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue. Request early check-in from the hotel in advance. Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury arrival experience. September weather in Prague is typically mild (15–20°C), ideal for evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Full private guided tour of Prague Castle Complex — the largest ancient castle in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral (including the Crown Jewels Chapel), the Old Royal Palace with Vladislav Hall, St. George's Basilica, and the Golden Lane. Book a skip-the-line private guide for an immersive 2.5-hour deep-dive into 1,000 years of Bohemian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) via Nerudova Street, browsing artisan boutiques and gallery spaces. Cross the iconic Charles Bridge — arrive mid-afternoon to enjoy it with fewer crowds than morning. Explore the Old Town (Staré Město) on the opposite bank, visiting the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) and the Gothic Church of Our Lady before Týn. Browse the Old Town Square at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Private evening river cruise on the Vltava aboard a premium charter boat — enjoy champagne, canapés, and illuminated views of Charles Bridge, Prague Castle, and the National Theatre as dusk falls over the city.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at your Hradčany boutique stay — enjoy a curated spread of local pastries, cold cuts, cheeses, and fresh juices in the hotel's intimate dining room.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lokál Malá Strana — a beloved upscale Czech brasserie serving perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell tank beer and traditional dishes like svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and roast duck.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — Prague's celebrated Michelin-starred restaurant offering an extraordinary tasting menu rooted in historical Czech recipes, with optional wine pairing. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle opens at 09:00; arriving early ensures the best experience before tour groups arrive. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the castle complex and Malá Strana involve significant cobblestone walking. Evening cruise should be pre-booked as a private charter for the full luxury experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — one of Europe's most significant and poignant historic districts. Tour the six synagogues (Old-New Synagogue, Pinkas Synagogue with its haunting Holocaust memorial inscriptions, Spanish Synagogue) and the Old Jewish Cemetery with its layered tombstones. A private guide is strongly recommended to fully appreciate the depth of history here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mucha Museum to explore the Art Nouveau masterworks of Alfons Mucha, followed by a walk along Pařížská Street — Prague's most luxurious boulevard lined with flagship designer boutiques (Louis Vuitton, Hermès, Bulgari). Optional: visit the Rudolfinum Gallery for a contemporary art exhibition. Relax with afternoon tea at the Grand Café Orient, a beautifully restored Cubist café.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music performance — Prague is one of Europe's premier cities for live classical music. Options include a concert at the Rudolfinum (Czech Philharmonic), the Municipal House (Smetana Hall), or an intimate chamber concert in a Baroque palace hall. Post-concert drinks at a sophisticated cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Eska — a celebrated modern Czech restaurant in the Žižkov district offering creative farm-to-table cuisine with a focus on fermentation, sourdough, and local seasonal ingredients. A favorite among Prague's culinary cognoscenti.
meals.dinner: Pre-theatre dinner at Alcron Restaurant (Radisson Blu Alcron Hotel) — an Art Deco gem with a Michelin Bib Gourmand, offering refined European cuisine and an outstanding seafood menu. Elegant and unhurried.

day_by_day.notes: Jewish Quarter entry requires a combined ticket; purchase online in advance to avoid queues. Check the Czech Philharmonic and Prague Philharmonia concert schedules well ahead and book seats in premium sections. Josefov is walkable from Old Town — comfortable shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Kutná Hora — a UNESCO World Heritage town 70km east of Prague, easily reached by private car (1 hour). Visit the extraordinary Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a medieval chapel decorated with the bones of 40,000 people, one of the most unique and haunting sites in all of Europe. Then explore the magnificent Gothic Cathedral of Saint Barbara, a rival in grandeur to St. Vitus in Prague.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by early afternoon. Visit the National Museum on Wenceslas Square (recently restored to its full Neo-Renaissance glory) for an overview of Czech natural history, culture, and national identity. Walk Wenceslas Square — the heart of modern Prague and site of pivotal 20th-century historical events — with your guide providing context on the 1968 Prague Spring and 1989 Velvet Revolution.
day_by_day.evening: Final Prague evening — enjoy a leisurely dinner followed by a nightcap at one of Prague's most atmospheric bars. Optional: visit the Hemingway Bar, widely considered one of the best cocktail bars in Central Europe, for a perfectly crafted pre-Prohibition era cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Early in-hotel breakfast before departure to Kutná Hora.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kutná Hora at Dačický Restaurant — a charming historic restaurant in a Renaissance building serving traditional Bohemian cuisine, including game dishes and local Kutná Hora beer.
meals.dinner: Farewell Prague dinner at Field Restaurant — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering an inventive, ingredient-driven tasting menu with a strong Czech identity and exceptional wine and non-alcoholic pairing options.

day_by_day.notes: Private car to Kutná Hora is the most comfortable option; trains also run regularly from Prague Main Station. The Ossuary can be intense — it is nonetheless a profoundly significant and extraordinary cultural site. Pack out of Prague hotel tonight or arrange luggage storage for early morning transfer to Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer or premium train (Railjet/EuroCity) from Prague to Budapest — journey is approximately 6.5–7 hours by train or 4.5 hours by private car/driver. Depart early morning. If traveling by train, enjoy the scenic Central European countryside from a first-class compartment with breakfast onboard. Arrive Budapest by early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your luxury Budapest hotel (recommended: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace or Párisi Udvar Hotel for a historic property). After settling in, take a private orientation walk along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) with views of Buda Castle, Chain Bridge, and the Pest embankment. Visit the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) — Budapest's magnificent iron-and-tile covered market — to browse local paprika, Tokaji wine, embroidery, and artisan food products.
day_by_day.evening: Evening stroll across the iconic Széchenyi Chain Bridge at dusk as the city lights illuminate. Dinner in the Belváros (Inner City) district.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Prague hotel before departure, or onboard the train in first class.
meals.lunch: Lunch onboard or at a rest stop en route, or upon arrival in Budapest — a light meal at Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square, Budapest's most historic and elegant café, established in 1858.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Costes Restaurant — Budapest's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a refined tasting menu of contemporary Hungarian cuisine with impeccable service and a superb wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Prague–Budapest private transfer or first-class train tickets well in advance. The Railjet operated by ÖBB/MÁV offers comfortable first-class seating. Alternatively, a direct flight (1 hour) is available if preferred, though the overland journey through Central Europe is itself a cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Danube to the Buda side for a comprehensive private guided tour of Buda Castle Hill. Visit Matthias Church — a stunning Gothic-Baroque hybrid with extraordinary Zsolnay tile roof patterns — and the Fisherman's Bastion for breathtaking panoramic views over the Pest skyline, Parliament Building, and the Danube. Explore the castle district's medieval streets, the Budapest History Museum, and the Hungarian National Gallery within the castle complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace gardens and descend by the historic Castle Hill Funicular. Cross back to Pest and visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the world's most beautiful legislative buildings — on a premium guided interior tour (book in advance). Marvel at the Crown Jewels of Hungary displayed inside.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury thermal spa experience at the Széchenyi Thermal Baths — the grandest of Budapest's famous bath complexes, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque palace in City Park. Book a private cabin and enjoy the thermal pools, steam rooms, and optional massage treatments in the early evening. Dinner in the Andrássy Avenue area afterward.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel's fine dining restaurant.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Alabárdos Restaurant in the Buda Castle district — an atmospheric medieval cellar restaurant serving elevated Hungarian cuisine with game, foie gras, and traditional gulyás reimagined for the modern palate.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Onyx Restaurant — Budapest's two-Michelin-starred flagship, located on Vörösmarty Square, offering a world-class Hungarian tasting menu with wine pairing from the legendary Tokaj and Eger wine regions.

day_by_day.notes: Book Parliament tours online well in advance — English tours sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Széchenyi Baths are open in the evening and considerably less crowded than daytime; a private cabin rental is worth the premium for a luxury experience. September evenings in Budapest are warm and pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and a profound monument to Budapest's once-thriving Jewish community. Tour includes the Hungarian Jewish Museum and the moving Heroes' Temple. Afterward, explore the Erzsébetváros (7th District) — Budapest's historic Jewish Quarter, now a vibrant cultural neighborhood with Art Nouveau architecture, independent galleries, and the famous ruin bar scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a guided interior tour of one of Europe's most opulent opera houses. Continue to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennium Monument, then explore City Park (Városliget), including the exterior of Vajdahunyad Castle.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — one of the finest opera venues in the world, with exceptional acoustics and lavish Neo-Renaissance interiors. Check the September program for opera, ballet, or orchestral performances and book premium seats in advance.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Borkonyha WineKitchen — a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant near St. Stephen's Basilica, celebrated for its creative Hungarian cuisine paired with an extraordinary selection of Hungarian wines. A true insider's Budapest experience.
meals.dinner: Pre-opera dinner at Kollázs Brasserie & Bar (Four Seasons Gresham Palace) — elegant brasserie cuisine in one of Budapest's most spectacular Art Nouveau interiors, with views of Chain Bridge. Post-opera nightcap at the hotel's sophisticated bar.

day_by_day.notes: Hungarian State Opera tickets should be booked as early as possible — the September season opening often features headline productions. Dress code for the opera is smart-formal. The Jewish Quarter walk can be self-guided with an audio guide or led by a private guide for deeper historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — visit St. Stephen's Basilica, Budapest's most important Catholic church, and ascend to the dome panorama terrace for a 360-degree view of the city. Browse the upscale boutiques and galleries around Váci Street and the Deák Ferenc area for last-minute gifts: Tokaji Aszú wine, Zsolnay porcelain, Hungarian embroidery, and fine paprika.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed farewell lunch near your hotel. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final coffee at the legendary New York Café — the most ornate and storied café in Budapest, decorated in extravagant Neo-Baroque style, often called 'the most beautiful café in the world.' Private luxury transfer to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Budapest. Reflect on an extraordinary 8-day journey through two of Central Europe's most magnificent capitals — Prague's Gothic spires and Baroque grandeur, Budapest's imperial boulevards and thermal heritage.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — take time to savor it.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Stand Restaurant — a Michelin-starred Budapest institution run by celebrated chef Szabina Szulló and Tamás Széll, offering deeply personal, ingredient-driven Hungarian cuisine that is among the finest expressions of the country's culinary identity.
meals.dinner: Dinner at airport or onboard flight, depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international flight departure for Budapest airport. Arrange private luxury transfer from hotel to airport. Consider purchasing a bottle of Tokaji Aszú 5 Puttonyos or Royal Tokaji as a premium souvenir — available at the airport duty-free or at specialty wine shops in the city center.
